subject: Live chat streaming latency spike — interim mitigations and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Reyes <ops@fastcart.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@fastcart.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in live chat latency — 09:05–09:40 PDT

Hi team,

We saw a sudden increase in interactivity latency on our FastCart help widget this morning between ~09:05 and 09:40 PDT. Users reported long pauses in streaming responses (several seconds vs sub-200ms baseline) and at least one automated session timed out and reconnected. This maps to increased token emission delay in our production traces.

Attached: a short trace and a zipped capture of logs. Can you confirm whether this was on your side and if there are any immediate mitigations we should apply? Our peak load was normal in terms of request count; the issue looks like token-level pacing.

We’re on a tight promo window and need quick guidance (retries, client-side backoff, temporary model switch) while you investigate.

Thanks,
Jordan
Site Reliability Manager
FastCart

Attachments:
- fastcart_incident_logs_1013.zip (zip)
- sample_trace_1013.json (json)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <ops@fastcart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in live chat latency — 09:05–09:40 PDT

Jordan — thanks for the quick heads-up and for sending the logs. Rafael and Laura are pulling traces now; prelims look like a transient token-emission backlog originating at the edge-to-serving handoff during a short control-plane flapping event. We’ll confirm root cause, but in the meantime here are safe, short-term mitigations you can apply immediately: 

1) Client-side change (recommended, immediate): add a 300ms inter-token jitter before showing a spinner and increase websocket ping timeout to 10s — this reduces perceived flakiness for users and avoids premature reconnections.
2) Fallback model: route streaming to a lower-latency variant we host (gpt-lite-128) for 30–60 minutes; code snippet attached.
3) Retry strategy: exponential backoff with a max of 2 retries for streaming handshake failures.

We’ll follow up with a fuller incident advisory and a mitigation package within 6–8 hours, plus any credit for downtime if warranted. Laura — can you scope a quick canary switch plan for FastCart? Rafael — please include a timeline for the fallback rollout and exact cause once you have it.

—Kimberly
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced in message: fastcart_fallback_snippet.txt (text)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <ops@fastcart.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in live chat latency — 09:05–09:40 PDT

Jordan — quick operational plan below. We did the following between 09:40–10:05 PDT and recommend these actions for your team if you want parity while our root-cause fix is deployed: 

A. Immediate actions we performed (completed):
- Canary switch: routed 100% of FastCart streaming traffic to gpt-lite-128 variant in us-west-2 for 25 minutes. Observed median token emission latency drop from ~1.2s to ~120ms.
- Edge reset: flushed the edge KV cache for the affected shard; eliminated stale routing entries.

B. Recommended quick client config (3–5 lines):
- Add a 250–350ms client-side spinner delay.
- On websocket close, wait 800ms and retry once; on second failure, fall back to polling with 2s interval for up to 15s.

C. Short-term rollout we can coordinate (if you approve):
- We can keep the gpt-lite-128 routing for the remainder of your promotional window (up to 48 hours) and monitor token latency. If you opt in, we’ll add a route tag and confirm CPU/GPU capacity.

D. Next steps from Redwood:
- Rafael to provide a root cause within 6 hours and an ETA for a deployable fix (config patch to edge routing controller).
- We’ll prepare a one-time service credit if the postmortem shows we missed an SLA target.

Let me know if you’d like us to proceed with keeping the fallback active; otherwise, implement the client changes now and we’ll follow up with the RCA and remediation schedule.

Laura Bennett
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Console

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <ops@fastcart.com>, Elena Soto <elena@fastcart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident advisory: 2026-10-13 token emission slowdown — summary & credit offer

Hi Jordan / Elena —

Thank you for your patience while we investigated. Below is the post-incident summary, the customer-facing mitigations we applied, and the next steps. We know this impacted your user experience during a high-traffic promotion and want to make this right.

Summary (what happened):
- Time window: 2026-10-13 09:05–09:40 PDT.
- Root cause: a transient control-plane routing flapping event caused a mismatch in edge->serving shard assignments, producing a token-emission backlog for affected sessions. The root trigger was an autoscaler race that briefly produced overlapping routing state during a controller leader election.

Actions we took (completed):
- Canary fallback: switched FastCart sessions to the lower-latency model variant (gpt-lite-128) between 09:40–10:05 PDT, restoring median token latency to ~120ms.
- Edge KV flush: removed stale routing entries from affected shards.
- Config patch: deployed a patch to the routing controller to make leader elections idempotent and avoid state overlap.

Customer mitigations recommended and implemented:
- Client: implemented a 300ms spinner/show-delay and adjusted retry timers as discussed.
- Ops: we documented an emergency rollback playbook to route to gpt-lite variants; you now have a route tag and can request it via support for emergency failover.

Impact & credit:
- Impact: an elevated median token latency for ~35 minutes affecting ~2.3% of sessions during the window.
- Credit: we are issuing a one-time usage credit equal to 10% of October 13 daily usage for FastCart. Finance will post this credit within 7 business days.

Preventive work (in progress):
- We’ll add stricter serialization to the autoscaler leader election path and a regression test that exercises overlapping routing states under heavy churn. Target: deploy to production by 2026-10-21.
- We’ll add an early-warning metric to the Console that detects token-emission pacing anomalies and fires at 2x baseline.

Attachments: included traces, timeline, and a runnable fallback snippet.

If you’d like a 30-minute post-incident review call, I can schedule Rafael and Karthik to walk through the technical details and the regression tests we’ll add. We appreciate the collaboration and are available to coordinate any further operational adjustments.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
